note: San Francisco Unified School District runs the city's public schools, from preschool and transitional kindergarten through grade 12, plus county schools and programs for students 18 to 22 with disabilities. A seven-member Board of Education, elected citywide, adopts the budget and sets policy. Charter schools, which SFUSD lists separately, come second, and City College of San Francisco, the public community college with its own elected Board of Trustees, is third.

issues.title: Board votes 5-2 to move toward neighborhood-based school assignment
issues.status: Draft policy due March 2027; final vote set for April 13, 2027
issues.summary: On October 13 the Board of Education voted 5-2 to have SFUSD develop a neighborhood-based assignment system for elementary schools, replacing the lottery. Under the proposed policy every family would be assigned to a neighborhood school based on their home address, and families would keep access to citywide specialized programs. Staff will update attendance boundaries, review each school's enrollment capacity, plan to improve school quality districtwide (including stable staffing and budgets at every school), and hold community engagement sessions. The Board is expected to review a draft policy in March 2027 and vote on April 13, 2027. The new system would take effect in October 2027 for students enrolling for the 2028-29 school year.

source.label: SFUSD press release, Oct 13, 2026

issues.title: What happens next on school assignment
issues.status: Study session Nov 10; board discussion Jan 12; vote April 13, 2027
issues.summary: SFUSD calls the October 13 vote a direction, not the final policy, and says nothing changes for current families. The final vote, set for April 13, 2027, is to cover attendance areas, citywide tiebreakers, and where language and special education programs are placed; sibling priority has not been decided. Next steps: Study Session 4 on school program decisions and tradeoffs (November 10), a board discussion of school program decisions (January 12, 2027), Study Session 5 on draft policy language and what families said (February 2), Study Session 6 on a near-final proposal (March 16), and Study Session 7 on the rollout plan (May 18). The district says community sessions in multiple languages will be held at schools and in neighborhoods through spring 2027, and public comment is taken before each study session on that meeting's topics. A fall family survey ran September 11 to October 9.

source.label: SFUSD School Reorganization page (updated Oct 23, 2026)

issues.title: How commissioners split on the enrollment vote
issues.summary: On October 13 the Board voted 5-2 for Option C, directing staff to draft a neighborhood-based enrollment policy. Students would first be offered a seat at a neighborhood school near home; families could also apply to citywide programs such as language pathways and K-8 campuses, without a guarantee. Commissioners Alida Fisher and Supriya Ray voted no and backed Option B, which would have let families apply to any school with open seats. Staff will work with demographers on attendance-boundary maps and tiebreakers. The change is meant to take effect for students entering elementary school in fall 2028; families would apply under the new rules in fall 2027.

source.label: KQED, Oct 14, 2026

issues.title: How the enrollment options were narrowed
issues.summary: At an October 6 study session the Board dropped Option A, leaving Options B and C, both of which guarantee a neighborhood seat. The SF Standard reported the final policy is scheduled for adoption April 13, 2027.

source.label: San Francisco Standard, Oct 6, 2026

issues.title: 2026-27 budget is balanced, with deficits projected in later years
issues.summary: The adopted budget projects $207,446,474 in Unrestricted General Fund revenue against $207,157,988 in spending and transfers. Its multi-year projection assumes 2% enrollment growth a year and shows deficits of $6,580,115 in 2027-28, $16,554,290 in 2028-29 and $24,002,844 in 2029-30, with the ending fund balance falling from $72,198,441 (34.85%) at the end of 2026-27 to $25,061,192 in 2029-30. In her budget message, Chancellor Messina wrote that strategic enrollment must be central to the college's strategy, "but enrollment alone will not solve the challenge."

methodology: Built November 4, 2026 from pages opened that day. SFUSD schools: the district's school directory, table view ("Showing 1 - 128 of 128 results", https://www.sfusd.edu/schools/directory/table), for names, grades, addresses and links. Level follows the directory's type: County School is shown as Continuation/Alternative, K-8 School as K-8, and schools with early education and elementary grades as Elementary. Two rows that are second campuses (Claire Lilienthal's K-2 Madison campus and Rooftop's 5-8 Mayeda campus) are folded into their schools, and The Academy - San Francisco @ McAteer is left out because its page says it is permanently closed, so 125 are listed. The Mandarin Immersion TK-8 School is listed with its fall 2027 opening (SFUSD press release, Sep 24, 2026). Grade 13 is explained from the AccessSFUSD, Project Search and Wallenberg Access pages. Individual school pages could not be opened (permission requests timed out), so principals are given only for the two AccessSFUSD programs whose pages were found through search. Per-school enrollment is the 2025-26 figure from four CDE school profiles (Sutro, Bryant, Visitacion Valley Elementary, Mission Education Center); DataQuest blocks automated reading and other profiles could not be reached, so the rest are blank. District enrollment is from Ed-Data (2025-26); SFUSD's 2025-26 Facts at a Glance figures are posted as images and could not be read. No per-pupil figure: CDE's current expense per ADA files are spreadsheets that could not be opened, and Ed-Data's finance tables load only in a browser. Test results: spring 2026 CAASPP results are now out, so they are used instead of 2025; the state figures are from CDE's CAASPP reporting site and the district figures from EdSource, because the district's all-students totals could not be reached on the state site. No district graduation rate is shown: no official class of 2025 figure for SFUSD could be opened (the state rate was 87.5%, CDE release of Nov 13, 2025). Board: the district's Board of Education page, board meeting calendar and School Reorganization page; BoardDocs minutes could not be read, so the only board decision listed from the last eight weeks is the October 13 enrollment vote (SFUSD press release) plus the charter petitions on the oversight page. Calendar: the 2026-27 district calendar PDF and Enrollment Key Dates page. Closings link: SFUSD posts closure notices, such as the February 2026 strike closures, under Public Announcements. Election results are preliminary (San Francisco Standard results page, updated Nov 4, 7 a.m.); the Department of Elections page could not be opened. Charter schools: SFUSD's student records list (updated Nov 3, 2026), the Charter Schools Oversight Committee page (updated Oct 27, 2026) and the CDE profile of The New School of San Francisco. City College: the FY2026-27 adopted budget, the 2026-27 catalog (locations and trustees), the Office of the Chancellor page, the 2026-27 academic calendar and spring 2027 instructional calendar, two college news releases, and The Guardsman. The trustees' meeting schedule, agendas and video are on a Diligent site whose address the college does not give, and spring 2027 registration dates were not posted on any college page that could be opened. Earlier items carried over from the live file keep their original sources (KQED Oct 14 and Sep 24, SF Standard Oct 6, SFUSD June 25 budget release).
